Data source overview:
This source is an overview page from AI Impacts (as of April 2017) that synthesizes evidence on AI timeline predictions across surveys, public statements, and written analyses, and summarizes methodological considerations about prediction accuracy and bias. It links to underlying datasets and analyses showing publication bias toward earlier predictions, differences between surveys and public statements, selection bias among experts, group differences, the non-validity of the Maes-Garreau law, and similarities between historical and contemporary predictions.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[84]
- Rationale: The source provides clear, enumerated claims about biases and differences in AI timeline predictions, plus references to datasets and surveys. I decomposed these into risks, mechanisms, insights, designs, implementations, validations, and actionable interventions, maintaining traceability to the closest section titles. Some interventions extend the text with moderate inference (marked via lower edge confidence and lifecycle/maturity) to make the content operational for AI safety planning. The JSON is validated for structural integrity, node/edge name matches, and connectedness.
- How to improve instructions: 
  - Allow a separate “governance/policy intervention” lifecycle taxonomy alongside model-development phases, since many AI safety-relevant interventions here are meta-forecasting and governance actions not well-captured by phases 1–5. 
  - Encourage explicit mapping from each validation finding to at least one concrete intervention template to standardize “motivates” edges across 500k sources.
  - Permit a “data infrastructure” intervention subtype to distinguish repositories/metadata standards from analytic interventions.
- Inference strategy justification: I used light-to-moderate inference to turn methodological findings (e.g., publication bias, survey vs statement differences) into concrete, governance-grade interventions (e.g., bias-adjusted aggregators, diversified surveys, robust scenario planning). Interventions align closely with the mechanisms and validations reported and rely on standard meta-analysis practices.
- Extraction completeness: All listed considerations (1–6) under “accuracy and bias” are represented as validation evidence and connected backward to implementation mechanisms and forward to interventions. The “predictions themselves” (surveys, public datasets, written analyses) are decomposed into implementation mechanisms and linked to findings. Competing hardware-vs-software analyses are captured to motivate software-inclusive modeling.
- Key limitations: The page is an index/outline; many details live on linked pages not fully quoted here, so evidential strengths are estimated conservatively. Interventions are governance-oriented and not native to the AI model lifecycle taxonomy (thus lifecycle=6). Quantitative effect sizes for bias corrections are not provided in the source.
